note: Read 2026-11-01 at the owner's word ("Build those first 3 starting with ledger first"; of the 21 countries read first: "It should cover across every country"; "Retry the blocked tax facts once all countries land"): the tax on a screen worker's pay in Papua New Guinea: a resident's income tax, social contributions, what is withheld at source, a non-resident artiste's withholding, an author's treatment, VAT and the tax year. Research and retry subagents (workbench/briefs/BRIEF-tax.md, BRIEF-tax-retry.md), every quote checked by the lead against its saved page.

figures.finding: A resident pays nothing on the first PGK 20,000 of taxable income, then 30% to 33,000, 35% to 70,000, 40% to 250,000 and 42% above; a non-resident pays 22% from the first kina; income tax is national (some provinces levy a head tax).

sources.said: The rates for residents are as follows: Taxable income (PGK*) Tax thereon (PGK) Tax on excess (%) 20,000 0 30 33,000 3,900 35 70,000 16,850 40 250,000 88,850 42
The rates for non-residents are as follows: Taxable income (PGK) Tax thereon (PGK) Tax on excess (%) 0 0 22 20,000 4,400 30 33,000 8,300 35 70,000 21,250 40 250,000 93,250 42
While some provinces have a 'head tax', Papua New Guinea does not have a local tax system.

figures.finding: The tax year is the calendar year; returns are due by 31 March of the next year; employees fully taxed at source need not file; provisional tax on other income is paid in three instalments.

sources.said: The tax year is generally the period 1 January to 31 December.
Annual income tax returns are generally due for lodgement by 31 March of the following year.

figures.finding: There is no social security; superannuation is compulsory for PNG citizen employees (6% employee, 8.4% employer, of gross basic salary) and voluntary for non-citizens.
figures.applies: Employees of employers of 15 or more

sources.said: Papua New Guinea does not have a social security system. However, there are compulsory superannuation contributions for PNG citizen employees (superannuation contributions are not currently required for non-citizen employees but may be made on a voluntary basis).
6.0% employee contributions (i.e. after-tax contributions). 8.4% employer contributions (i.e. pre-tax contributions).

figures.finding: Salary or wages tax is assessed fortnightly from standard tables and is a final tax; employers remit it monthly.

value.employee: fortnightly salary or wages tax, final

sources.said: Salary or wages income is subject to salary or wages tax and is subject to fortnightly assessment of tax, regardless of the employer's actual pay period. The tax assessed is a final tax and is determined by reference to standard rate tables.

figures.finding: From 1 January 2026 a payment to a non-resident entertainer or entertainment group bears a final non-resident tax of 10% of the gross; royalties 10% (30% to an associate).
figures.applies: Non-residents without a PNG permanent establishment (ITA 2025 s 14)

sources.said: Non-resident tax (NRT) under Section 14 of ITA 2025 imposes a final tax (via withholding under Part 10) on specified categories of PNG-source income derived by non-resident persons (individuals or corporations) where the income is not attributable to a PE in Papua New Guinea.
Entertainment fees (payments to non-resident entertainers or entertainment groups): 10%.

figures.finding: Royalties for the use of copyright paid to a non-resident bear 10% final non-resident tax; the Small Business Tax regime excludes professional services; no special regime for resident authors was found.

sources.said: as consideration for the use of, or right to use, any copyright, patent, trademark, design, model, plan, secret formula, or process

figures.finding: GST is 10% on most supplies; the registration threshold is PGK 250,000 of turnover in an income year.

sources.said: The GST rate is 10% and applies to most goods and services supplied in Papua New Guinea.
2% of turnover for a small business that derives less than the registration threshold for GST (currently PGK 250,000 in an income year)
